unverified: How other browsers display it: not claimed.
The figure from the 2021 Chrome study (11 percent) is not used in this version.
The sequence of the example case (Example Bank, the address 135x-examplebank.example, direct debit, code request, times) is invented and marked as an example.
The BSI speaks of a TAN (transaction number); localised as 'one-time code for a payment'.
Fallback localised: the German blocking hotline 116 116 from S3 is replaced by 'call your bank', which S3 also names.

Newly checked 02.11.2026: S2 (a TAN request without a transaction of your own is a clear sign of a fake page) and S3 (criminals harvest passwords on fake pages; contact your bank and check transactions).

What exactly does the little padlock in the address bar tell you?

Wednesday, 4:40 p.m. Your bank's login page, with the padlock at the top.
hook_candidates.visual: clock, the login page arrives as a paper card, the padlock line is marked

beats.spoken: Wednesday, 4:40 p.m. A link in an email opens your bank's login page. In the address bar: the padlock.
You check. The padlock: there. The address: starts with https. The design: as always. Looks secure. But according to the Chrome team, nearly all phishing sites show the padlock too.

fact.text: Nearly all phishing sites show the padlock too.

beats.spoken: What do you do? A: The padlock is there, so you sign in. B: You check the certificate: valid. C: You read the address, character by character. Remember your choice.

options.text: Read every character of the address

beats.spoken: Let's play out A. You sign in. Then the page asks for a one-time code for a payment you never made. According to the BSI, that's a clear sign of a fake, and your login details are already gone.

The right answer is C. Germany's BSI advises checking every link before you open it. Be suspicious of the bank's name with unusual numbers in front. On A: the padlock only shows an encrypted connection. On B: scammers get certificates too.

card.title: Read the address
card.sub: bank name plus odd characters? Stop.

beats.spoken: Already signed in? Then call your bank straight away to block access, and check your transactions with them.
Encrypted doesn't mean genuine. Read the address. What would you have picked? Tell me in the comments.
